Explain one difference between insertion and bubble sorts in how they reorder data. [4 marks]
Insertion sort takes a key [1] and inserts it into a growing sorted section [1]. Bubble sort compares adjacent pairs [1] and swaps out-of-order neighbours over passes [1].

On paper, explain how the third value could be inserted to finish ordering the original array.
k.a: Original first insertion: [1,4,3]; prints 1 then 4. With [6,2,5], first insertion makes [2,6,5]; prints 2 then 6. For original third value 3, shift 4 right and insert 3 to make [1,3,4]. The code models one insertion, not a full generic sorter.
